newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Senate advances proposed casino regulations.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Senate advances proposed casino regulations.

text.p: The Michigan Senate has approved a regulatory package requiring Detroit casinos to pay annual service fees totalling $25 million and to reimburse the state for gaming board operations, an assistant to the majority leader said Monday.

The Senate package advanced Thursday creates a framework for regulating future Detroit casinos and leaves intact a provision allowing the city to exercise a preference for awarding licenses included in last November's referendum, said Jay Yaney, assistant to Sen. Dick Posthumus, R-Alto.
The referendum permits Detroit to have up to three land-base casinos after review of the applications by both the city and state.

Mayor Dennis Archer's preliminary application circulated earlier in June calls for at least two casinos to be located in the Washington Boulevard-Detroit Edison district downtown and no more than one in the Greektown district.
A mayoral task force had rejected Greektown as a casino development site. The "preferred parties" in the referendum are local entities, Greektown Casino LLC and the Atwater Group.
Applicants must pay $50,000 for preliminary consideration and another $250,000 if they are selected as a finalist and would like to continue pursuing a license.
The annual state service fees would be tied to the consumer price index and an annual municipal service fee of $4 million or 1.25 percent of adjusted gross receipts would also be levied.

Senators also advanced proposed requirements for Michigan Gaming Control Board members, added investigatory powers for the board and expanded factors the board may consider in reviewing a licensing request.
Elected officials could not accept campaign contributions from managerial employees or anyone with more than one percent interest in a casino as well.
The regulatory plans next go to the Michigan House for consideration.
Preliminary applications with the city are due August 1 and selection of finalists is expected on August 22. Three finalists will be selected to negotiate a development agreement on November 10.
A number of groups have announced interest in developing a casino, including Detroit businessman Don Barden, owner and operator of the Majestic Star Casino in Gary, Ind.
Circus Circus Enterprises Inc has joined with the Atwater Group.
MGM Grand Inc, Mirage Resorts Inc and Harrah's Entertainment Inc have also expressed interest.
